en.explanation:
Einstein's photoelectric equation is given by

where is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons, is Planck's constant, is the frequency of the incident radiation, and is the work function of the metal (the minimum energy needed to eject an electron).

If you plot against , you will get a straight line with slope (Planck's constant) and y-intercept (the negative of the work function). The slope of the line (which is ) does not depend on the intensity of the radiation or the type of metal used. Instead, it is a universal constant.

Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option D: The slope is the same for all metals and independent of the intensity of the radiation.
